Container.Name: filearr-stepca
Container.Overview:
Private certificate authority (smallstep step-ca) for filearr's distributed agent fleet. OPTIONAL: install it only if you set Agent Auth Mode to mtls-header or both on the filearr container. Every enrolled agent gets its own short-lived client certificate from this CA and presents it to the filearr-caddy container, which verifies it and forwards the already-verified identity to filearr.
FIRST BOOT auto-creates a fresh CA from the DOCKER_STEPCA_INIT_* variables below and prints two things ONCE into the container log: the root certificate fingerprint and the CA administrative password. Copy BOTH out of the log immediately — the fingerprint goes into the filearr container's CA Root Fingerprint, and the password is what you need later to read the provisioner key and change certificate lifetimes.
THE DATA PATH IS CA PRIVATE KEY MATERIAL. Back it up, and understand that recreating this container from scratch mints a NEW root — at which point every certificate it ever issued stops validating and every agent must be re-enrolled.
NETWORKING: two topologies are supported. DEFAULT — every container on one user-defined Docker network, addressing each other by NAME; create it once with docker network create filearr. ALTERNATIVE — every container fully bridged (Network Type: Custom br0) with its own fixed LAN IP, in which case filearr-caddy's CA Upstream and this container's CA DNS Names both take IPs instead. Both are documented field by field: https://pwsh.github.io/filearr/deployment/unraid/#step-0-networking
Container.Requires: docker network 'filearr'; the filearr container with Agent Auth Mode mtls-header or both

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: CA root + intermediate keys, provisioner state, and the issuing database. PRIVATE KEY MATERIAL — this is the one path in the stack whose loss cannot be repaired by re-scanning or rebuilding: a new CA means re-enrolling every agent. Use the DIRECT pool path (/mnt/cache/appdata/...), never the array, and include it in your backups. scripts/backup.sh archives the compose equivalent of this directory.

Config.Name: CA Port
Config.Description: OPTIONAL host mapping. Leave EMPTY in the standard topology: agents reach the CA through the filearr-caddy container's raw layer-4 passthrough on ca.<your-domain>, and filearr-caddy talks to this container over the 'filearr' network by name (or by its fixed LAN IP on a fully bridged br0 stack, where port 9000 is reachable on that address whether or not this field is set). Map it only for local debugging (step ca health).

Config.Name: CA Name
Config.Description: Human-readable CA name baked into the root certificate subject on FIRST BOOT ONLY. Changing it later does nothing — the CA already exists.

Config.Name: CA DNS Names
Config.Description: Comma-separated names the CA's OWN TLS certificate is valid for. FIRST BOOT ONLY. Add the public CA hostname you will publish through filearr-caddy — e.g. localhost,filearr-stepca,ca.example.com — because the layer-4 passthrough hands agents this container's real certificate, not a proxy-terminated one. On a fully bridged (br0) stack the container name resolves to nothing: use localhost,ca.example.com plus this container's fixed LAN IP.

Config.Name: Provisioner Name
Config.Description: Name of the JWK provisioner created on FIRST BOOT. Must match CA Provisioner on the filearr container (default filearr-agents on both).

Config.Name: Remote Management
Config.Description: Enables step-ca's admin API so certificate lifetimes and provisioner claims can be changed with 'step ca provisioner update' instead of hand-editing ca.json. Keep true — the documented setup uses it. Note that with remote management on, the provisioner key is encrypted under the ADMINISTRATIVE password from the first-boot log, not the CA key password.

Config.Name: Init Password
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Sets the CA administrative password on FIRST BOOT instead of letting step-ca generate one and print it to the log. Use this if you would rather choose the secret than scrape it out of container output. Leave empty to auto-generate — then read it from the log immediately (docker logs filearr-stepca | grep -i password) and store it.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone (affects log timestamps; certificate validity is always UTC)
